operatorApproval.notes:
The scan at 46a7109b built its record list from unit directories x generation directories and opened nothing else: 119 of the 228 tracked records. Flipping status to FAIL in T09/T09.handoff.json -- a tracked record, one whose correction X15's own PR body announces -- left it printing RESULT ok with exit 0 (C1 of X16/logs/03). It accepted a fabricated negative-control record as a canonical child (C2, the probe from review-650 finding P5); it printed canonical records no parent names as a count it then ignored, which is why #650 could merge with four broken links and seven unnamed records; and the 66 payload fixtures under */fixtures/ were invisible to it.

This unit: every tracked record is read and counted where it lives (in generations=119, in unit directories=41, elsewhere=68); an unnamed canonical record is an ORPHAN-OFFENCE unless AUDIT/chain-declaration.json says why, and a declaration that stops applying is a STALE-DECLARATION, so B00's chain-head exception and the tampered control's hash waiver have to keep earning their place; named controls can no longer satisfy a forward link; and each payload fixture must equal another record of its own unit apart from handoffHash. No runtime code and no test changed -- test:unit is 6784 tests, 6779 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped, the same as at X15's commit (X16/logs/05).

Two limits this unit does not remove. RESULT ok still does not certify that the trail is one connected walk; the chain walk plus the declared exceptions do, and the comment above the exit status says so; taskAuthorityHash is carried from X15 and reproduces from nothing stored in the repo; and nothing runs these scans on push: this repo has no .github/workflows since 85b1b064 removed them, so the claim in #650's body and #650's review that CI runs AUDIT/integrity-scan.mjs is false, and main can drift into an offending state with nothing noticing. That is recorded as X17's first task.
